subject: industrial-systems
audience: FE Industrial & Systems candidates and industrial engineering students
title: The Cell That Needed 4 Machines, Not 3
featured_title: THE CELL THAT NEEDED 4 MACHINES, NOT 3

presentation.challenge: Three machines looked sufficient at 100% theoretical availability. At the planned 80% utilization, the cell required four machines.

practice.primary_question: How are demand, processing time, available shift time, and planned utilization combined to size machine capacity?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Dividing required processing time by nominal shift time and ignoring the stated planned utilization before rounding to a whole-machine count.
also_relevant_to: Manufacturing, Service, and Other Production Systems

case_dna.target_misconception: Three machines are enough because 270 parts×5 min/part divided by 480 min/shift is only 2.81 machines.
case_dna.why_plausible: The nominal-time calculation is correct at 100% utilization, but the stated capacity plan allows only 80% of each machine's shift time for productive processing.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Required work is 1350 machine-min/shift. Effective capacity per machine is 480×0.80=384 min, so 1350/384=3.516 and four machines are required.

problem_statement: A production cell must complete 270 parts per shift. Each part requires 5.0 minutes of processing on one identical machine. A shift provides 480 minutes per machine, but capacity planning limits scheduled utilization to 80%. A note divides 1350 required machine-minutes by 480 and rounds 2.81 up to three machines. Determine the required number of machines.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: Nominal shift time was mistaken for planned productive capacity.
gates.prompt: How much planned productive time is available per machine?

options.label: Use N=ceil[demand×time/(available time×utilization)]
options.reason: The utilization factor reduces planned productive capacity per machine.

options.label: Use N=ceil[demand×time/available time]
options.reason: That assumes 100% utilization despite the stated 80% planning limit.

options.label: Multiply required work by utilization before dividing by time
options.reason: Utilization applies to available capacity, not to the processing work required.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the required machine count
gates.prompt: Enter the whole number of machines.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the machine requirement
gates.hint: Each machine contributes only 384 planned productive minutes per shift.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Three machines exceed the utilization plan

cards.text: Planned productive capacity per machine=480×0.80=384 min/shift.
Three machines would require 1350/(3×480)=93.75% actual utilization, above the 80% plan.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the capacity-planning note
report: C1. Required processing work is 1350 machine-min/shift.
C2. Each machine has 480 nominal minutes per shift.
C3. Therefore three machines satisfy the stated 80% utilization plan.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: The nominal shift duration is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It ignores that only 80% of nominal machine time is planned as productive capacity.

evidence_choices.label: 1350/(480×0.80)=3.516 → 4 machines
evidence_choices.reason: This applies the stated utilization factor before rounding up.

correction.template: The cell requires {machines} machines under the 80% utilization plan.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Operate with only three machines at the same 80% utilization
gates.constraint: Keep processing time at 5.0 min/part and shift length at 480 min.

options.label: Reduce demand to 230.4 parts/shift or less
options.reason: Three machines provide 3×480×0.80=1152 productive minutes, equal to 230.4 parts at 5 min each.

options.label: Keep demand at 270 parts/shift
options.reason: That requires 93.75% utilization from three machines.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Size another machine group
gates.prompt: Demand is 180 parts/shift, processing time is 6 min/part, shift time is 480 min, and planned utilization is 75%. How many machines are required?

options.label: 2 machines
options.reason: Two machines provide only 720 planned productive minutes.

options.label: 4 machines
options.reason: Four are not required by the stated workload and utilization.

gates.explanation: Size machine count from workload divided by effective planned capacity per machine.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the machine-capacity calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that planned utilization reduces usable capacity and must be applied before rounding the required machine count upward.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Nominal shift time was treated as fully productive capacity.

seo.seo_title: Machine Capacity and Utilization Sizing | FE Industrial E-085
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Industrial & Systems Case E-085: 270 parts at 5 min each with 480 min shifts and 80% planned utilization require 4 machines.
seo.excerpt: Machine count should be based on effective planned capacity, not nominal shift time when a utilization constraint is specified.
seo.direct_answer: Required workload is 270×5=1350 machine-min/shift. Effective capacity per machine is 480×0.80=384 min/shift. Therefore 1350/384=3.516, so four machines are required.

faqs.q: How do you include utilization when sizing machines?
faqs.a: Divide required workload by available time multiplied by the planned utilization, then round up.

faqs.q: What utilization would three machines need in this case?
